newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate up on primary paper maturity.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate up on primary paper maturity.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up 75 basis points to 18.15 percent at mid-morning trade on Thursday.
Dealers said speculative pressure had the upper hand and shunned a strong peso and U.S. long bond that would normally have tended to push rates down.
"The market is speculative as primary Cetes fall due today and some dealers are holding on their cash until midday," a fixed-income analyst said.
Another analyst said market liquidity was under additional pressure from term instruments falling due.
"Some dealers may have gone short on liquidity and others are putting them under pressure," he said.
Dealers said a strong peso could well allow secondary rates to fall after liquidity pressures had subsided.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were 0.05 of a centavos softer at 7.8315/7.8335 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper were down 30 basis points at 18.50 percent.
Liquidity of 1.807 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
